purpose: A voltage-controlled high-power electronic switch. Unlike BJTs which consume continuous base current, a MOSFET gate draws zero steady current and has near-zero internal resistance (R_DS(on)). It allows a 5V or 3.3V Arduino pin to switch 5A to 50A+ loads like 12V/24V LED strips, motors, and heating elements at high-speed PWM with virtually zero heat.

whenToUse.scenario: High-Current Loads (1A to 50A+): 12V/24V LED Strips, Motors, Heaters
whenToUse.why: Standard BJTs (like 2N2222) top out at 800 mA. Relays cannot be switched fast with PWM. A MOSFET handles massive currents (5A to 50A) with negligible heat thanks to milliohm-level internal resistance.

whenToUse.scenario: High-Speed PWM Dimming and Motor Speed Control
whenToUse.why: Mechanical relays can only switch 10–20 times per second and will quickly wear out. MOSFETs switch millions of times per second, making them the industry standard for smooth LED brightness dimming and DC motor PWM speed control.

whenToUse.scenario: Battery-Powered IoT Devices (Zero Gate Power Consumption)
whenToUse.why: BJTs waste 5 mA to 20 mA of continuous control current to stay turned on. A MOSFET gate is insulated by glass (silicon dioxide)—once charged, it consumes 0.000 mA static current, preserving battery life.

whenToUse.scenario: THE CRITICAL RULE: Always Choose 'Logic-Level' MOSFETs!
whenToUse.why: The #1 beginner trap in Arduino electronics! Standard power MOSFETs (like the infamous IRF520 or IRFZ44N) require 10V at the Gate to turn on fully. When driven by a 5V or 3.3V Arduino pin, they only partially open, act like a heating element, and can catch fire. You MUST choose a LOGIC-LEVEL MOSFET (look for an 'L' in the part number, like IRLZ44N or IRLB8721) which turns on fully at 3V to 4.5V.
whenToUse.recommended: IRLZ44N, IRLB8721, FQP30N06L (Avoid IRF520 for 5V direct drive!)

whenToUse.scenario: Always Add a 10 kΩ Gate Pull-Down Resistor
whenToUse.why: When the Arduino boots or resets, its pins are high-impedance inputs. The MOSFET gate acts like a tiny sensitive capacitor and will pick up static noise, causing your motor or laser to randomly turn ON. A 10kΩ resistor from Gate to GND ensures it stays firmly OFF until your code actively drives it.
whenToUse.recommended: 10 kΩ pull-down resistor from Gate to GND

basics.title: Gate (G), Drain (D), Source (S)
basics.text: The three pins of a MOSFET. Gate is the control switch (connected to Arduino). Drain connects to the negative side of your load. Source connects to GND (for N-Channel). Current flows between Drain and Source.

basics.title: N-Channel vs P-Channel
basics.text: N-Channel is a Low-Side switch (Source to GND, Drain to Load negative). It is used in 95% of microcontroller projects because it is cheap, low-resistance, and easy to drive directly. P-Channel is a High-Side switch (Source to VCC, Drain to Load positive).

basics.title: R_DS(on) — On Resistance
basics.text: The resistance between Drain and Source when the MOSFET is fully turned on. Good logic-level MOSFETs have R_DS(on) under 0.020 Ω (20 milliohms). At 5A load, 20 mΩ drops only 0.1V and wastes only 0.5 Watts of heat—no heatsink needed!

basics.title: Gate Protection (Series Resistor + Pull-Down)
basics.text: Place a small 100Ω to 220Ω resistor between the Arduino pin and the Gate to limit the microsecond inrush current charging the gate capacitor. Place a 10kΩ resistor between Gate and GND to keep the MOSFET safely OFF during boot.

types.name: N-Channel Logic-Level MOSFET
types.looks: Standard black TO-220 package with metal mounting tab (Pins: 1-Gate, 2-Drain, 3-Source).
pros: Directly driven by 5V Arduino Nano pins with zero driver ICs
Handles 10A+ without needing a bulky heatsink
cons: Low-side switching (load negative is separated from ground when off)

types.name: P-Channel Logic-Level MOSFET
types.gateThreshold: Negative V_GS (Turns on when Gate pulled low)
types.looks: Same TO-220 package; part numbers like IRL9530 or FQP27P06.
pros: High-side switching: load always stays securely grounded to common chassis
cons: If the load voltage exceeds 5V (e.g. 12V), requires a small NPN transistor to pull the gate to ground safely

types.name: Small Signal MOSFET (2N7000 / BS170)
types.looks: Tiny half-cylinder TO-92 package, identical in shape to a 2N2222 BJT.
pros: Perfect for low-power sensors, I2C level shifting, and tiny relays
cons: Higher ON-resistance (1.2–5 ohms), so not suited for heavy currents (>500 mA)
